ja: だいろくじゅうろくかい

p.src: Now Bao Er's wife gave him a playful slap and laughed. “There was some truth in it to begin with, but then you embroidered it with all that nonsense until it no longer holds together at all. You hardly sound like someone in the Second Master's service; that nonsense of yours sounds more like something from Baoyu's side of the household.” Second Sister You was about to question him further when Third Sister You suddenly asked with a smile, “That Baoyu of yours—apart from attending school, what does he do?” Xing'er laughed. “You had better not ask about him, Madam. Even if I told you, you might not believe me. Of all our young masters, he alone has never attended a proper school, though he is already fully grown. From our forebears down to the Second Master, who in our family has not spent ten hard years studying by a cold window? Yet he alone dislikes books. He is the Old Lady's darling. His father used to discipline him, but nowadays even he no longer dares. He behaves crazily all day long; no one understands what he says or knows what he is doing. Outsiders see his handsome, refined appearance and naturally suppose him intelligent, never guessing that he is fair without but muddied within; when he meets people, he cannot utter a word. The best that can be said of him is that, though he never attended school, it is remarkable that he can recognize a few characters. He neither practices letters nor learns martial arts, and he is afraid of meeting people; all he likes is romping among the maids. Besides, he has neither firmness nor severity. When he sees us and is in a good mood, he forgets all distinctions of rank and romps about with everyone; when he is displeased, we each go our own way and he pays no attention to us. Even if we remain seated or lying down when we see him, he ignores it and does not rebuke us. So no one is afraid of him. We behave as freely as we please, and somehow everything passes.” Third Sister You laughed. “When a master is lenient, you servants behave like this; when he is strict, you complain. That shows how impossible you are to please.” Second Sister You said, “We always thought well of him, but is that really what he is like? What a pity for one so finely endowed.” Third Sister You said, “Sister, do not believe his nonsense. We have seen Baoyu more than once or twice. It is true that his conduct, speech, eating, and drinking have something feminine about them, but that is only because he has always lived among the women inside the house. But if you call him foolish, in what respect is he foolish? Sister, remember when we were together during the mourning? That day, just as the monks came in to circle the coffin, we were all standing there, and he alone stood in front, blocking their way. People said that he had no manners and no sense of what was proper. But afterward, did he not quietly tell us, ‘You do not understand, sisters. It was not that I failed to see what was proper. I thought the monks were filthy, and I feared their odor might offend you.’ Then, while he was drinking tea, you asked for some too, and the old serving woman was about to pour it into his bowl. He hurriedly said, ‘I have soiled that one by drinking from it. Wash another and bring it.’ From those two incidents, as I watched him closely, I realized that however he behaves before girls, there is always a reason for it. He simply does not conform very well to outsiders' conventions, and so they fail to understand him.”

p.src: Second Sister You heard this and laughed. “From what you say, it seems you two are already perfectly matched in heart and affection. Why not simply betroth you to him? Would that not be splendid?” With Xing'er present, Third Sister could not answer and merely lowered her head to crack melon seeds. Xing'er laughed. “Judging by looks, conduct, and character, you would indeed make a fine pair. The trouble is that he already has someone intended for him, though nothing has yet been made public. In time, he is certain to be promised to Miss Lin. But because Miss Lin is often ill, and because they are both still young, the matter has not yet been broached. In another two or three years, once the Old Lady speaks, no one will possibly object.” As they were talking, Long'er returned and said, “The Master has business to attend to—a highly confidential matter. He is sending the Second Master to Ping'an Prefecture. The Second Master will leave within three to five days, and the round trip will take at least half a month. He cannot come today. He asks the Elder Madam to settle that matter promptly with the Second Young Lady, so that when he comes tomorrow, a final decision can be made.” Having said this, he took Xing'er away with him.

p.src: Second Sister You then ordered the gate shut and retired early, questioning her younger sister throughout the night. Jia Lian did not arrive until the following afternoon. Second Sister You urged him, “Since you have serious business, why hurry over here again? Whatever you do, do not let me delay your affairs.” Jia Lian replied, “It is nothing much. It is merely that, of all things, another distant assignment has come up. I shall leave at the turn of the month and will not return for half a month.” Second Sister You said, “In that case, go with an easy mind. You need not worry about anything here. Third Sister has never been one to change her mind from morning to night. Since she has said that she has repented, she will certainly mend her ways. She has already chosen the man she wants; you need only abide by her wishes.” When Jia Lian asked who it was, Second Sister You laughed. “The man is not here at present, and no one knows when he will return. One must admire her discernment. She herself declared that if he does not return for a year, she will wait a year; if he does not return for ten years, she will wait ten years. If he dies and never returns, she would rather shave her head and become a nun, abstaining from meat and reciting the Buddha's name until this life is over.” Jia Lian asked, “Who can it be who has so completely won her heart?” Second Sister laughed. “It is a long story. Five years ago, when our maternal grandmother celebrated her birthday, Mother took us to her home to offer our birthday respects. The family had engaged a troupe of amateur players, and among them was a young man named Liu Xianglian who played the romantic male lead. She took a fancy to him and now refuses to marry anyone else. Last year we heard that Liu Xianglian had got into trouble and fled. Do you know whether he has returned yet?” When Jia Lian heard this, he exclaimed, “No wonder! I wondered what sort of man she could have chosen, and it turns out to be him! She certainly has a discerning eye. You do not know Second Brother Liu. He is a remarkably handsome fellow, but extremely cold in manner and heart; he treats almost everyone with utter indifference. He gets along best with Baoyu. Last year, after he beat that fool Xue, he was too ashamed to face us and disappeared somewhere for quite a while. Later I heard someone say that he had returned, but I do not know whether it is true. We shall know as soon as we ask Baoyu's boys. But suppose he has not returned? He wanders as aimlessly as drifting duckweed, and who knows how many years it may be before he comes back? Would she not be wasting her youth waiting in vain?” Second Sister You said, “Our Third Sister does whatever she says she will do. Whatever she has decided, we need only let her have her way.”

p.src: While the two were still talking, Third Sister You came over and said, “Brother-in-law, set your mind at ease. We are not the sort to say one thing while thinking another; what we say, we mean. If the man named Liu comes, I shall marry him. From this day onward, I shall eat vegetarian food and recite the Buddha’s name, devoting myself solely to Mother’s care. When he comes, I shall marry him; if he does not come in a hundred years, I shall devote myself to religious practice.” As she spoke, she snapped a jade hairpin in two. “If a single word of mine proves false, may I be like this hairpin!” With that, she returned to her room and thereafter truly neither acted nor spoke in any way contrary to propriety. Jia Lian could do nothing more. After discussing the household affairs for a while with Second Sister, he returned home to consult Xifeng about his departure. Meanwhile he sent someone to ask Mingyan, but Mingyan said, “I really know nothing about it. He probably has not come yet; if he had, I would certainly know.” He also asked Liu’s neighbors, who likewise said that he had not returned. Jia Lian had no choice but to report this to Second Sister. As the day of his departure drew near, he announced two days beforehand that he was setting out, but first went to stay two nights with Second Sister, intending to leave quietly on his long journey from there. He saw that the younger sister had indeed become a different person and that Second Sister managed the household diligently and prudently, so there was no longer any need for concern.

p.src: Early that morning he left the city and took the main road toward Ping’an Prefecture, traveling by day and lodging by night, drinking when thirsty and eating when hungry. He had traveled for only three days when, while on the road, he saw a caravan of pack animals approaching. Among them was a party of masters and servants, some ten riders in all. When they drew near, he saw that they were none other than Xue Pan and Liu Xianglian. Jia Lian was greatly astonished and hurriedly urged his horse forward to meet them. After they had all exchanged greetings and inquiries about one another since parting, they entered an inn to rest and talk. Jia Lian said with a smile, “After that commotion, we were busy trying to reconcile the two of you, but who would have thought Brother Liu would vanish without a trace? How is it that you two are together today?” Xue Pan laughed. “There truly are strange wonders in this world. My assistants and I had been away trading goods since spring, and our return journey had been peaceful all the way. But the day before yesterday, after we entered the borders of Ping’an Prefecture, we encountered a band of robbers who seized all our goods. Then, quite unexpectedly, Second Brother Liu arrived from the other direction. He scattered the robbers, recovered our goods, and even saved our lives. He would accept no reward from me, so we swore brotherhood, pledging our lives to one another, and now we are traveling to the capital together. From now on, we shall be as close as brothers of the same blood. At the fork ahead we shall part ways. Two hundred li to the south lives an aunt of his, whom he intends to visit. I shall go on to the capital first and settle my own affairs; then I shall find him a house and arrange a good marriage for him, so that we may all live comfortably together.” When Jia Lian heard this, he said, “So that is what happened! You had us worried for several days.” Then, hearing him speak of finding a marriage, he hastily added, “I happen to know of an excellent match for Second Brother.” He then told them how he himself had married a lady of the You family and now wished to marry off her younger sister, though he omitted the fact that Third Sister You had chosen Liu herself. He also warned Xue Pan not to tell anyone at home for the present; once a son had been born, they would naturally come to know. Xue Pan was delighted. “You should have done this long ago. All of this was my cousin’s fault.” Xianglian hastily laughed and said, “You are getting carried away again. Hold your tongue.” Xue Pan at once fell silent, then said, “If that is the case, this marriage must certainly be arranged.” Xianglian said, “I have always vowed that I would marry only a woman of peerless beauty. But in view of the generous regard shown me by you honorable kinsmen, I shall no longer insist on so much. Decide as you see fit, and I shall obey in everything.” Jia Lian laughed. “Words alone are no proof. Once Brother Liu sees her, you will know that my wife’s younger sister is without equal in beauty and character, past or present.” Xianglian was overjoyed. “If you speak so highly of her, then after I have visited my aunt, I shall be in the capital by the middle of the month at the latest. Shall we settle the matter then?”

p.src: Jia Lian laughed. “Then let your word and mine seal the matter. Still, I cannot quite trust you, Brother Liu. You wander about like duckweed on the water, leaving no trace behind. If you should be delayed and fail to return, would you not ruin the young lady’s prospects? You must leave some betrothal token.” Xianglian replied, “How could a true man ever break his word? I have always been poor, and besides, I am traveling. How could I have a betrothal gift with me?” Xue Pan said, “I have suitable things here already. I shall prepare a gift for Second Brother to take with him.” Jia Lian laughed. “There is no need for gifts of gold or silk. It must be something that belongs personally to Brother Liu. Its value does not matter; I merely wish to take it back as proof of his pledge.” Xianglian said, “If that is what you require, I have nothing else. This sword is for my defense and cannot be removed. But in my traveling bag I have another sword, one of a paired set known as the Mandarin Duck Swords. It is a treasure handed down in my family, which I dare not use on my own authority and merely carry with me for safekeeping. Brother Jia, please take it as my pledge. Though my nature may be as restless as running water and falling blossoms, I would never willingly part with this sword.” When he had finished speaking, he opened his bag, took out the sword, and presented it respectfully to Jia Lian. Jia Lian ordered a servant to put it away. They drank a few more cups, then each mounted his horse, exchanged farewells, and resumed his journey. Indeed: The generals do not dismount; each rides on toward his own destiny.

p.src: Now one day Jia Lian reached Ping'an Prefecture, met with the military governor, and concluded his official business. The governor instructed him to be sure to return around the tenth month, and Jia Lian accepted the order. Early the next day he hurriedly set out for home, stopping first to visit Second Sister You. Little did he know that after his departure, Second Sister You had managed the household with the utmost care and propriety, keeping the doors shut every day and paying no heed whatever to affairs outside. Her younger sister proved a woman of unwavering resolve: apart from attending upon her mother and elder sister each day, she kept quietly to her proper place and lived contentedly within her means. Though at night she lay alone beneath a solitary quilt and was unaccustomed to such loneliness, she had put everyone else out of her mind and thought only of Liu Xianglian's early return, when the great affair of her life might be settled. When Jia Lian entered and saw how matters stood, he was delighted beyond measure and felt deeply grateful for Second Sister's virtue. After they had exchanged the customary greetings, Jia Lian told them how he had met Xianglian on the road, then took out the Mandarin Duck Swords and handed them to Third Sister. Third Sister examined them. The scabbard was adorned with intertwined dragons and kui-dragons and glittering jewels; when she pulled the hilt, she discovered that it held a matched pair of swords. One was engraved with the character “yuan,” the other with “yang”; cold and gleaming, they resembled two limpid streaks of autumn water. Overjoyed beyond expectation, Third Sister quickly put the swords away and hung them above the bed in her embroidered chamber. Each day she gazed at them, smiling to herself that her future was now secure. Jia Lian stayed two days, then returned to report the fulfillment of his father's instructions and went home to greet the entire household. By then Xifeng had almost completely recovered and had resumed going about and managing affairs. Jia Lian also told Jia Zhen about the matter. Jia Zhen had lately found new companions and had put the whole affair out of his mind. He left Jia Lian to decide everything, but, fearing that Jia Lian might not manage alone, he could not avoid giving him another thirty taels of silver. Jia Lian took the money and gave it to Second Sister to prepare her younger sister's trousseau.

p.src: As it happened, Xianglian did not enter the capital until the eighth month. He first paid his respects to Aunt Xue and then met Xue Ke, from whom he learned that Xue Pan, unaccustomed to the hardships of travel and unable to adapt to the climate, had fallen ill at home as soon as he entered the capital and was being treated by a physician. When Xue Pan heard that Xianglian had come, he invited him into his bedchamber to meet him. Aunt Xue no longer dwelt on their former grievance but remembered only his recent kindness, and both mother and son thanked him profusely. They also discussed his marriage, saying that every necessary preparation had been completed and only the choice of an auspicious date remained. Liu Xianglian was deeply grateful as well.

When Xue Pan heard that Xianglian had come, he invited him into his bedchamber to meet him.

p.src: The next day he went to see Baoyu, and when the two met, each delighted in the other's company like a fish returned to water. Xianglian asked about Jia Lian's secret taking of a second wife. Baoyu laughed and said, “I heard Mingyan and the others talking about it, but I have not seen her myself, and I dared not meddle too much. I also heard Mingyan say that Second Cousin Lian had questioned you most earnestly. What did he have to say?” Xianglian told Baoyu everything that had happened on the road. Baoyu laughed and exclaimed, “What joyful news! What joyful news! Such a beautiful woman is hard to find. She truly is a peerless beauty in any age and well worthy of a man like you.” Xianglian said, “If that is so, surely they know no lack of suitable men. Why should they have thought only of me? Besides, I have never been especially close to him, so he had no reason to concern himself so deeply on my behalf. We were in such haste on the road, yet he pressed me again and again to settle the engagement then and there. Surely the bride's family would not chase after the groom's? I began to have doubts and regretted leaving those swords as betrothal tokens. That was why I later thought of you: I wanted to ask you closely and learn the truth of the matter.” Baoyu said, “You are usually such a discerning man. Why did you present the betrothal gift if you were going to grow suspicious afterward? You always said that all you wanted was a peerless beauty. Now that you have found one, that should be enough. Why entertain further doubts?” Xianglian said, “If you did not know about his marriage, how do you know that she is a peerless beauty?” Baoyu replied, “She is one of the two younger sisters whom Sister-in-law Zhen's stepmother brought with her. I spent a whole month in their company there. How could I not know them? They truly are a pair of irresistible beauties—and their family name happens to be You, too.” Hearing this, Xianglian stamped his foot and cried, “This is bad! I absolutely cannot go through with it. In your Eastern Mansion, nothing is clean except those two stone lions at the gate; I fear even the cats and dogs are tainted. I will not be the cuckold who takes another man's leavings.” At these words, Baoyu flushed red. Ashamed of his indiscretion, Xianglian hurriedly bowed and said, “Forgive me—I spoke recklessly. Please, whatever you do, tell me what her character is truly like.” Baoyu laughed. “Since you know so much already, why come and ask me? By your reckoning, perhaps even I am not clean.” Xianglian laughed and said, “It was only that I lost my head for a moment. Please do not take it to heart.” Baoyu laughed. “There is no need to mention it again. Your apology only shows how considerate you are.” Xianglian bowed and took his leave. He considered seeking out Xue Pan, but the man was bedridden with illness and, besides, was too impetuous; it would be better to reclaim the betrothal gift directly. His mind made up, he went straight to find Jia Lian. Jia Lian was in the new residence. When he heard that Xianglian had come, he was overjoyed and hurried out to welcome him, then ushered him into the inner room to meet old Madam You. Xianglian merely bowed to her and addressed her as “honored aunt,” referring to himself as her junior. Jia Lian was astonished to hear him speak so formally. As they drank tea, Xianglian said, “In the bustle of my travels I acted too hastily. Who could have known that in the fourth month my aunt had already arranged a bride for me, leaving me no grounds on which to refuse her?”

p.src: If I complied with you, elder brother, and went against my aunt, it would hardly be right. Had the pledge consisted of gold or silk, I would not dare ask for it back; but this sword was handed down by my grandfather, so I beg you to return it to me. Jia Lian felt distinctly uncomfortable on hearing this and replied, “A betrothal is a binding agreement. It is made precisely to prevent either party from changing their mind. How can anyone enter or withdraw from a marriage at will? You must think it over further.” Xianglian smiled. “Though you say so, I am willing to accept blame and punishment, but I could never obey you in this matter.” Jia Lian was about to argue further when Xianglian rose and said, “Let us sit outside and talk, brother. This is not a convenient place.” Third Sister You heard every word clearly from her room. She had waited so long and with such difficulty for him to come; now that he had suddenly changed his mind, she knew he must have heard something at the Jia residence and regarded her as a shameless, wanton woman unworthy to be his wife. If she allowed him to go outside and tell Jia Lian that he was breaking off the engagement, Jia Lian would surely have no way to deal with it, and she herself would be left utterly humiliated. As soon as she heard Jia Lian propose going outside with him, she hurriedly took down the sword, concealed its female blade inside her bent arm, and came out saying, “There is no need for you to go outside and discuss it further. Here is your betrothal gift.” Tears pouring down like rain, she offered Xianglian the sword and scabbard with her left hand, while with a sweep of her bent right arm she drew the blade across her throat. Alas, “the peach blossom was crushed, strewing the ground with red; the jade mountain toppled, never again to rise.” Her fragrant spirit and orchid-pure nature drifted away into the boundless dark, no one knew where. Everyone was so terrified that they rushed frantically to save her. Old Madam You wailed aloud, cursing Xianglian between her cries. Jia Lian seized Xianglian and ordered the servants to bind him and take him before the authorities. Second Sister You hastily checked her tears and instead tried to dissuade Jia Lian. “You are making too much trouble. No one threatened or forced her to die; she took her own life. What good would it do to hand him over to the authorities? You would only stir up trouble and bring shame upon us. Better let him go and spare ourselves further trouble.” Jia Lian no longer knew what to do, so he released his hold and told Xianglian to leave at once. But Xianglian would not move. Weeping, he said, “I never knew she was such a virtuous wife, so unyielding in honor. Worthy of reverence—truly worthy of reverence!” Xianglian supported her corpse in his arms and wept bitterly for a long while. After a coffin had been bought, he watched her body being placed inside, then bent over the coffin and wept bitterly once more before finally taking his leave.

p.src: Once outside, he had nowhere to go. Dazed and silent, he brooded over what had just happened. Third Sister You had been so beautiful and so unyielding in honor; his remorse came too late. As he walked on, one of Xue Pan’s young servants appeared to be looking for him to take him home, but Xianglian remained lost in thought. The servant led him into a bridal chamber, which was furnished with the utmost elegance. Suddenly he heard the tinkling of jade pendants, and Third Sister You entered from outside, holding the paired Mandarin-Duck Swords in one hand and a register in the other. Weeping, she said to Liu Xianglian, “For five years I waited for you with a foolishly devoted heart. I never expected you truly to be so cold of heart and countenance; with my death I have repaid this infatuated love. I have now received the command of the Goddess of Disenchantment to go to the Land of Illusion in the Great Void and revise the records of all the ghosts of love listed there. I could not bear to leave without farewell, and so I came to see you once more. From this day on, we can never meet again.” With that, she turned to leave. Unable to let her go, Xianglian hurried forward to seize her and question her, but Third Sister You said, “I came from the Heaven of Passion and depart through the Realm of Passion. In a former life I was mistakenly beguiled by passion; now, having awakened in shame from passion, I have no further bond with you.” As soon as she finished speaking, a fragrant breeze arose, and she vanished without a trace. Xianglian awoke with a start, uncertain whether it had been a dream. Opening his eyes, he saw neither the Xue family’s young servant nor the bridal chamber, but only a ruined temple; beside him sat a cross-legged Taoist picking lice from his clothes. Xianglian rose, bowed respectfully, and asked, “What place is this? And what, Immortal Master, are your honored name and religious title?” The Taoist laughed. “Even I do not know what place this is or who I am. I merely came here to rest my feet for a while.” At these words, Liu Xianglian felt a chill as though ice had pierced his bones. Drawing the male blade, he swept away all three thousand strands of worldly vexation with a single stroke, then followed the Taoist away, and no one knew where they went. The sequel will be revealed in a later chapter.
